subject: Localized storage commitments and tenant wipe process discussion
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cedarbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cedarbridge Security <security@cedarbridge.com>
Date: 2028-09-12T08:14:00Z
Subject: Clarify EU-localized storage & proof-of-delete for VPC deployment

Hi Ben / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this call last week. As we prepare to onboard Cedarbridge's tenant into a private VPC deployment, the security team asked for two concrete items we need before signing: 1) an explicit statement about where customer-controlled storage will be provisioned (region/availability zones) and 2) the operational evidence we can expect when Cedarbridge requests a full tenant wipe (what artifacts, timing, and attestation we will receive).

Specifically: 
- We need confirmation that all persistent customer data (models, embeddings, logs, snapshots) for our tenant will remain in the EU (Frankfurt region) and not be replicated outside the region unless we explicitly authorize it.
- We need a short checklist of the wipe steps (object deletion, snapshot removal, key rotation, KV cache eviction), an expected timeline for each step, and a signed attestation template we can use for our compliance records.

Can you share an ops-level description and the attestation template? Also indicate any limitations (e.g., backups retention windows, snapshots in immutable archives) we should be aware of.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of InfoSec
Cedarbridge Health

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-12T12:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Clarify EU-localized storage & proof-of-delete for VPC deployment

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front: yes, Cedarbridge's customer-controlled storage will be provisioned in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) by default for this Private/VPC deployment and we will not replicate data outside the region unless you provide written authorization.

Attached are two items to start: an "EU Residency Statement" that lays out our default storage and replication commitments, and an initial "Tenant Wipe Playbook" that describes every step we run during a full tenant deletion. Highlights below:

- Region binding: customer buckets, object stores, and model artifact volumes are created in your dedicated project in eu-central-1. Control-plane metadata remains in a private control plane we host in the same region for this engagement.
- Backups & snapshots: automated snapshots are retained for up to 30 days by default. Snapshots are region-local and not cross-region by default. If you require a shorter retention window at contract start, we can configure that.
- Wipe process (summary): 
  1) Quarantine tenant access (0-15m) — revoke tokens and network ACLs.
  2) KV cache flush (15-60m) — in-memory and on-disk caches cleared; ephemeral caches are not persisted.
  3) Object deletion (1-6h) — delete S3-like objects and metadata; soft-delete flags removed.
  4) Snapshot removal & GC (up to 24-72h) — scheduled background GC to remove immutable snapshots depending on retention policies; we can shorten this via manual override.
  5) Key rotation & KMS policy revoke (immediate) — customer keys can be rotated or disabled; if using customer-managed KMS, we can trigger revocation together with you.
  6) Attestation and evidence package (by EOD next business day) — we provide a signed CSV listing deleted object prefixes, snapshot ids removed, and timestamps.

I attached the two files for your review: EU-Residency-Statement.pdf and tenant-wipe-playbook-v1.docx. Let us know if you want more conservative defaults (e.g., 7-day snapshot retention instead of 30).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: EU-Residency-Statement.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: tenant-wipe-playbook-v1.docx (DOCX)]

Date: 2028-09-13T09:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Clarify EU-localized storage & proof-of-delete for VPC deployment

Elena / Ben —

Quick technical clarifications to supplement Ben's playbook: 

- Storage surfaces covered: model artifact volumes (block store), object store (S3-compatible for user data), and long-term archives. We configure the deployment so all of these are bound to the customer project in eu-central-1.
- Snapshot GC note: if snapshots are encrypted and stored in an immutable archive (rare), manual reclamation may require a short maintenance window; we'll surface any such objects in the evidence package. By default we avoid immutable cold archives for customer-owned VPC storage unless requested.
- KV caches & runtime state: runtime KV caches are flushed on wipe and the process is synchronous for in-memory caches and best-effort for local SSD spill; we mark the tenant as wiped only after cache flush confirmation.
- Third-party telemetry: we do not send tenant data to external analytics services. Operational telemetry (metrics/traces) is telemetry-only and redacted at tenant granularity; it does not contain user data or model payloads.

I've attached an ops checklist that maps each wipe step to the log signals you will receive and the expected evidence artifacts (object deletion audit entries, snapshot IDs, KMS key IDs).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops-wipe-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

Ben / Karthik —

This is helpful. Two follow-ups before we loop procurement in: 
1) Can Redwood produce a one-page attestation template that we can retain in our SOC records? It should include timestamps, list of deleted prefixes/snapshot ids, and the signature of an authorized Redwood officer.
2) If Cedarbridge requests an immediate wipe (e.g., contract termination with 24h notice), what is the minimum realistic time to completion for the evidence package? We need an SLA to put in the MSA.

If you can provide the attestation template and a proposed completion SLA (X hours for deletion confirmation, Y hours for full artifacts), we can get procurement moving. Ideally we'd have something we can click to sign (DocuSign or equivalent).

Thanks,
Elena

Elena —

Attached is the one-page attestation template (EU-Residency-Statement.pdf updated) and a signed handover statement (signed-eu-handover-statement.pdf) that we can run through DocuSign. Proposed SLA for an initiated tenant wipe with evidence package: 

- Deletion confirmation (object and token revocation): within 6 hours of initiation for standard-size tenants (<5TB active objects).
- Full evidence package (deleted object prefixes, snapshot ids removed, KMS actions, audit logs): delivered within 24 hours of initiation (EOD next business day for requests initiated late in day).

If you need a 24-hour hard SLA for both confirmation and full evidence (instead of our proposed 6h/24h), we can include that as a contract commitment for an enterprise SLA tier.

Next steps: I'll send the DocuSign envelope to your security contact; once signed we'll update the deployment defaults to the conservative settings you requested (snapshots 7d retention).

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
